description.narrative:
The Grassroots Green Council project aims to secure formal political representation for marginalised youth in Sheema, Uganda, ensuring their environmental and economic needs directly influence municipal decision-making.
The project will mobilise 15 young leadersfrom vocational and environmental cohorts to form a Youth Green Council (YGC). The YGC will receive targeted training in municipal budget analysis and policy advocacy. They will research current environmental budget allocations (focusing on waste management) and author an evidence-based Advocacy Brief.
The youth will then formally engage local authorities in Kabwohe Town through a Public Consultation Dialogue, aiming to secure a permanent, institutionalised consultation slot for the YGC. This outcome will ensure that thevoices of young women and environmental workers transition from being excluded from policy discussions to becoming mandatory partners in shaping Sheema's climate resilience and green transition agenda.
Project Goal To institutionalise youth policy representationwithin the Sheema Municipal Council, ensuring the voices of marginalised young people are integrated into environmental planning and resource allocation for the local Green Transition.
Project Objectives Theproject will achieve this goal through three main objectives over 12 months:
1. Capacity Building: To train 15 marginalised youth leaders (the Youth Green Council) in municipal budget analysis and evidence-based advocacy, empowering them with the technical skills required to engage local governance structures.
2. Policy Advocacy: To produce and formally submit an evidence-based Advocacy Brief
3. Structural Representation: To secure a written commitment from the Sheema Municipal Council establishing a permanent, formal consultation slot for the Youth Green Council, ensuring future youth participation in the municipal policy cycle
Activities The following activities are structured across fourphases to achieve structural policy change:
· Phase I: Mobilization <(>&<)> Training (M1–M3)
o Establish the 15-member Youth Green Council (YGC) from NWMEG’s cohorts.
o Conduct specialised Policy Analysis Training with a Local Governance Expert on how to read, interpret, and critique the municipal budget.
· Phase II: Research <(>&<)> Advocacy Output (M4–M6)
o Lead a Youth-Led Budget Review to identify policy and resource allocation gaps related to local environmental infrastructure (waste, drainage) in Kabwohe Town.
o Draft, design, and finalise the professional Advocacy Brief outlining the youth's official policy demands.
· Phase III: Formal Engagement (M7–M9)
o Formally submit the Advocacy Brief to the Sheema Municipal Council and key planning officers.
o Host a high-profile Public Consultation Dialogue in Kabwohe Town, bringing the YGC to the table with municipal councillors and technical staff to present their findings directly.
· Phase IV: Institutionalization <(>&<)> Global Link (M10–M12)
o Secure a Written Commitment from the Municipal Council granting the YGC a permanent, annual consultation slot in the local budget process.
o Facilitate the mandatory youth participation in the AU-EU Global Learning Event to share local lessons and build international networks.

participating-org.narrative:
The Nyanga Waste Management Group (NWMEG) is a youth-led, registered Community-Based Organisation (CBO) based in Sheema Municipality, Uganda, dedicated to addressing local socio-economic and environmental challenges through practical action and policy advocacy.
Vision: To harness technical and digital innovation to cultivate economically secure and environmentally resilient communities, empowering youth to lead sustainable development in Sheema Municipality.
Mission: To mobilise, train, and empower young people through sustainable technical skilling (waste management) and civic advocacy, ensuring their economic independence and protecting their fundamental rights within the community.
Core Objectives:
To equip marginalised youth with vocational and technical skills (including waste management, tailoring) necessary for economic independence. To implement efficient, youth-led technical solutions for localised community challenges (including waste management). To secure youth representation in municipal resource allocation and policy formulation processes, ensuring that youth needs are integrated into local governance. Core Values: NWMEG’s work is guided by: Youth Leadership, Environmental Stewardship, Inclusivity <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> Gender Equity, and a commitment to Innovation and Action in problem-solving.
